name: Differentiable alignment and structured DP losses: smoothed-max DP (Mensch & Blondel, ICML 2018), soft-DTW (Cuturi & Blondel, ICML 2017) and soft-DTW divergence (Blondel, Mensch & Vert, AISTATS 2021), Drop-DTW (NeurIPS 2021), Deep Declarative DTW (DecDTW, ICLR 2023), neural linear-chain CRF / HMM layers (incl. hybrid CNN-CRF stereo 2017, SGM-Nets 2017)
authors_org: A. Mensch, M. Blondel (Inria / NTT, later Google); M. Cuturi, M. Blondel; M. Blondel, A. Mensch, J.-P. Vert (Google); N. Dvornik, I. Hadji, K. Derpanis, A. Garg, A. Jepson (Samsung AI Centre Toronto); M. Xu, S. Garg, M. Milford, S. Gould (QUT / ANU); P. Knobelreiter, C. Reinbacher, A. Shekhovtsov, T. Pock (TU Graz); A. Seki, M. Pollefeys (Toshiba / ETH)
year: 2017-2023 (soft-DTW 2017, CNN-CRF stereo 2017, SGM-Nets 2017, Mensch & Blondel 2018, soft-DTW divergence 2021, Drop-DTW 2021, DecDTW 2023)
venue_link: Mensch & Blondel, ICML 2018, arXiv:1802.03676 (https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.03676). Soft-DTW, ICML 2017, arXiv:1703.01541. Differentiable Divergences Between Time Series, AISTATS 2021, arXiv:2010.08354. Drop-DTW, NeurIPS 2021, arXiv:2108.11996 (https://github.com/SamsungLabs/Drop-DTW). DecDTW, ICLR 2023, arXiv:2303.10778 (https://openreview.net/forum?id=UClBPxIZqnY). CNN-CRF stereo, CVPR 2017, arXiv:1611.10229. SGM-Nets, CVPR 2017.
code_availability: Public: tslearn / pysdtw / Maghoumi pytorch-softdtw-cuda (soft-DTW); SamsungLabs/Drop-DTW; DecDTW code linked from the paper [uncertain]; VLOGroup/cnn-crf-stereo (C++/CUDA); Torch-Struct (Rush 2020) provides linear-chain CRF log-partition, marginals, argmax and sampling in PyTorch. A banded linear-chain forward-backward over 400 TVT states is ~50 lines of PyTorch.
evidence_level: Peer-reviewed (ICML, AISTATS, NeurIPS, ICLR, CVPR). Read at abstract / summary level plus known method details; no application to geosteering found. Internal evidence from our repo: the 2nd-place AnchorCNN is a locally normalised, teacher-forced path model (MEMM-like) scoring 5.94 ft holdout, and the post-hoc forward-backward decode on ConvNeXt posteriors failed (16 focus wells 11.32 -> 12.14).
extreme_summary: Replace the hard max/min in a dynamic program (Viterbi, DTW, CRF forward) with a smoothed max (log-sum-exp or other strongly convex regulariser) so the DP value and its argmax relaxation become differentiable; gradients of the smoothed value are the expected path (edge marginals). This lets a network learn unary and pairwise potentials end-to-end against a path-level loss, i.e. a trained version of the continuity decode, with Drop-DTW adding skip costs and DecDTW giving exact-path gradients.
task_definition: Structured prediction over monotone or Markov paths: sequence labelling (Viterbi/CRF), time-series alignment and averaging (DTW), step localisation in video (Drop-DTW), audio-to-score alignment and visual place recognition (DecDTW), stereo disparity (CNN-CRF, SGM-Nets). For us: predict the TVT-level path over 345 MD columns given the cost image, with a learned Markov transition between neighbouring columns.
inputs: Unary scores from a network (for us the ConvNeXt/FastViT per-column logits over 400 TVT levels) plus pairwise scores: a fixed or learned transition kernel over dTVT per column, optionally conditioned on column features (inclination, predicted dip, GR contrast), as SGM-Nets predicts penalties from image patches.
target_parameterisation: Discrete state = TVT level (0.5 ft bins) per MD column; path = sequence of levels. DTW variants instead align lateral GR samples to typewell depths monotonically, which is wrong for laterals that go up and down through strata; the linear-chain CRF over TVT levels is the right form (non-monotone, like the 2nd-place DP and the patents in A04).
output_representation: Path-level distribution: log-partition, per-column marginals (forward-backward), pairwise marginals, MAP path (Viterbi), or samples (forward-filtering backward-sampling). The per-column marginals are directly comparable to our current softmax.
architecture: CNN backbone -> unary potentials theta_t(s) (T=345 columns x S=400 levels) + transition potentials A_t(s, s') (banded, |s - s'| <= ~80 bins i.e. 40 ft, translation-invariant kernel k_t(ds) predicted per column by a small head, as a Toeplitz/banded convolution) -> differentiable forward-backward layer (log-semiring, i.e. Mensch & Blondel with negentropy regulariser) -> marginals. Soft-DTW: DP over an alignment cost matrix with soft-min. Drop-DTW: extra drop states with learned drop costs. DecDTW: continuous-time DTW solved as an inner optimisation, gradients by implicit differentiation. CNN-CRF stereo: CNN unaries + contrast-sensitive pairwise terms, trained with a structured SVM loss.
core_mechanism: Smoothed Bellman recursion: max_Omega(x) = log sum exp(x) (entropy) or sparsemax-like (squared L2) turns DP into a differentiable operator whose gradient w.r.t. potentials equals expected edge occupancies. With the entropic smoother, the forward value is log Z of a linear-chain CRF and the gradient is the CRF marginal, so training by CRF negative log-likelihood of the true path gives gradient = model marginal - one-hot truth. Crucially the unaries are learned jointly with the transitions, so they become local evidence (likelihood-like potentials) rather than already-contextualised marginals; the global normalisation then produces calibrated path marginals. Globally normalised CRFs also avoid the label bias / exposure bias of locally normalised teacher-forced models (MEMM), which is what the 2nd-place AnchorCNN is.
training_objective: Options: (a) CRF NLL of the discretised true TVT path: -score(y) + log Z (log Z by forward algorithm); (b) marginal (posterior) likelihood / CE on forward-backward marginals against our existing soft typewell targets, which matches a per-point metric better (Kakade et al. 2002 alternative objective); (c) expected-RMSE loss on the marginal mean sum_s gamma_t(s) x_s (differentiable through forward-backward), i.e. the existing 'regression' term applied after the CRF; (d) soft-DTW divergence / Drop-DTW as alignment losses (not the right structure for non-monotone laterals); (e) structured SVM (CNN-CRF stereo). Recommended for pooled RMSE: (b)+(c), optionally with a small (a) weight.
decoding: Forward-backward marginals then expectation (RMSE-consistent). Viterbi / MAP path is mode-seeking. Forward-only filtering is what the 2nd-place dp_expected_level does (exact for its locally normalised chain because the move field already sees the whole image). DecDTW returns the exact optimal path.
metric_consistent_decode: Marginal expectation from forward-backward is Bayes-optimal for pooled RMSE if the CRF marginals are calibrated; Viterbi, argmax and DecDTW's optimal path are mode-seeking and would raise RMSE on ambiguous wells.
evidence_scope: Whole lateral jointly (every column's marginal conditions on all unaries through the chain), single well plus typewell. Longer-range dependence than first-order (e.g. constant drift slope) needs a second-order state (level, slope), as in the silver structural tracker (A15).
prefix_conditioning: Natural: clamp the chain to the known heel TVT at the first unknown column (initial distribution = delta or narrow Gaussian), as posterior_fb_decode.py and dp_expected_level already do; the prefix columns can also be clamped observations.
propose_vs_select: Single structured output (marginals), but forward-filtering-backward-sampling yields coherent path samples that can feed a propose + rerank stage (item B04) or the 2nd-place-style shape gate.
physical_constraints: Continuity (banded transitions), learned step-size distribution per column, optional asymmetric up/down penalties (SGM-Nets style), optional second-order smoothness via augmented state; monotonicity is imposed only by DTW variants and is inappropriate here.
dataset: Mensch & Blondel: CoNLL NER and machine translation attention; soft-DTW: UCR time-series; Drop-DTW: CrossTask, COIN, YouCook2 instructional videos; DecDTW: audio-to-score, Oxford RobotCar / Nordland visual place recognition; CNN-CRF: Middlebury 2014, KITTI 2015. No well-log datasets.
synthetic_to_real: Not addressed. For us the transition kernel could be fitted on real training wells only (TVT change per 32 ft column: std 0.78 ft, q99 2.0 ft, max 8.6 ft measured on training wells), while unaries learn from the synthetic-heavy mix; a real-only fine-tuning stage for the pairwise head is cheap.
metric_and_performance: Mensch & Blondel: structured attention/NER results competitive with standard CRF training; soft-DTW: better barycenters and forecasting than Euclidean loss; Drop-DTW: SOTA weakly supervised step localisation on CrossTask/COIN; DecDTW: SOTA audio-to-score alignment and place recognition vs soft-DTW; CNN-CRF stereo: strong Middlebury/KITTI results with shallow CNNs and no post-processing. None of these are RMSE-on-ambiguous-path numbers.
comparability: Not comparable externally. Internal anchors: ConvNeXt expectation 4.84 ft (FastViT distilled) / 5.47 ft (60 ep); AnchorCNN locally normalised path model 5.94 ft; post-hoc FB decode worse than expectation on 16 focus wells.
validation_protocol: Fixed benchmark splits in the papers; not applicable to our well-level holdout.
inference_budget: Banded forward-backward: 345 sequential steps of B x 400 x ~161 multiply-adds, a few ms per well on GPU and ~tens of ms on CPU; the 2nd-place repo measured its DP decode at 28.7 ms/sample batched. Training memory: store alpha/beta (345 x 400 floats per well) or use a custom autograd that recomputes; negligible vs the U-Net.
repeated_layers: A trained chain helps only if pairwise evidence disambiguates bands: a band switch requires a large jump, which the learned transition makes expensive, so a path that is consistent with the heel anchor and continuous is preferred. Because training calibrates the product unary x transition, it should not over-commit as the post-hoc decode did; but if the correct band is also reachable by a smooth path, the chain cannot choose it and the marginal stays bimodal (correctly, for RMSE).
drift: First-order transitions do not penalise a constant-slope drift (each step is small). Needs a second-order state (level x slope bins, or a transition conditioned on a predicted dip per column) to encode 'one straight-line drift per well'; the state-space grows (400 x ~9 slope bins) but stays tractable.
uncertainty_and_calibration: CRF marginals are calibrated under the model when trained by likelihood; our post-hoc product of already-contextualised marginals double-counts evidence and over-sharpens, which is the mechanism behind the failed decode. Calibration can be checked with the existing per-bin reliability tools and a temperature on unaries/transitions fitted on training wells.
where_to_use: A CRF head after the ConvNeXt/FastViT decoder logits: alignment_logits become unaries, a small head predicts per-column transition kernels, forward-backward produces marginals that replace the softmax in the alignment CE, regression and GR_penalty losses (experiments/arch/seq_NN_train.py) and in the expectation decode (seq_NN_holdout_eval.py). Also applicable to the AnchorCNN: replace its teacher-forced local CE with global normalisation.
error_mode_targeted: Band confusion (~51%), in particular blend (15%) and wrong_mode picked after a spurious jump; drift (~25%) only with a second-order (slope) state.
gap_vs_our_implementation: What we do: per-column independent softmax trained with per-column soft CE + expectation regression + GR_penalty; the U-Net's receptive field gives implicit context but no explicit pairwise consistency; the post-hoc forward-backward in kaggle_1st_place/solution/posterior_fb_decode.py multiplies the network's per-column POSTERIORS (already conditioned on neighbouring columns) by a fixed Gaussian-mixture transition kernel fitted on training wells, which treats marginals as independent likelihoods, double-counts shared evidence and over-sharpens toward whichever band has more mass near the anchor (hence 'wins big where it locks onto the right band and loses where it locks onto a wrong one'). The 2nd-place AnchorCNN is a trained path model, but locally normalised and trained by teacher forcing on the true path only (anchor_loss in kaggle2ndplace/src/gr2tvt_model.py), then decoded by forward filtering or sampled rollouts; it never sees off-path states during training except via the distillation experiment. Gap: nobody in our stack trains unaries and transitions JOINTLY under a globally normalised path likelihood or a marginal-based loss. That is exactly what Mensch & Blondel / neural CRF offer: the unaries learn to be local evidence and the transitions learn what continuity is worth, so the chain's marginals are calibrated by construction instead of hand-tuned (sig1, sig2, w2 in kernel()). DTW-family losses (soft-DTW, Drop-DTW, DecDTW) are NOT a direct fit because they assume monotone alignment; their contribution is Drop-DTW's idea of skip states (faults / missing GR) and DecDTW's exact-path gradients, both secondary.
proposed_experiment: E0 (cheap check of the double-counting hypothesis, no training): in posterior_fb_decode.py add a 'tempered emissions' option e = p^tau with tau in {0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5} (fitting tau and the kernel on TRAINING-well posteriors, which requires dumping training wells with seq_NN_posterior_dump.py), run on posterior_all.npz for all 155 holdout wells. If some tau beats the raw expectation by more than the 0.39 ft noise floor, that already proves pairwise structure adds information once double counting is removed. E1 (main, trained CRF head): new module experiments/arch/seq_NN_crf.py with a banded log-space forward-backward (log-sum-exp over a +-80 bin window via unfold, custom autograd or checkpointing), initial state clamped at the heel TVT, transition kernel k_t(ds) = softmax over 161 offsets predicted from decoder features pooled per column (initialise to the training-well dTVT histogram). Config flags in seq_NN_cfg.py: crf_head=True, crf_band_bins=80, crf_kernel='learned'|'fixed', crf_nll_weight (0 or 0.05). In seq_NN_train.py route extra['alignment_logits'] through the CRF and apply the existing alignment soft CE, regression and GR_penalty to the CRF marginals (loss (b)+(c)), plus optional CRF NLL of the discretised true path. Decode: marginal expectation. Control: same config with crf_head=False, same seed, 150 epochs, 2 seeds each, seq_NN_holdout_eval.py on 155 wells; also report the focus-well subset used by posterior_fb_decode.py for continuity with the negative result. E2 (if E1 helps): second-order state (level x 9 slope bins) for drift; FastViT student with the same CRF head, KD on CRF marginals.
implementation_effort: Medium: the banded forward-backward and its memory-efficient backward are the only new code (~150 lines with tests against brute force on tiny grids); masking variable-length suffixes and the prefix clamp are already solved in posterior_fb_decode.py and dp_expected_level. E0 is low effort. Second-order state is medium-high.
gpu_cost: E1 adds a sequential 345-step loop per batch (~5-15% step-time overhead [uncertain]) and O(345 x 400) activations per well; fits the RTX 5060 8 GB with the current batch size; a 150-epoch run costs about the same as a normal run plus overhead. E0 is CPU only.
distillation_compatibility: Good: KD on output posteriors becomes KD on CRF marginals (or on unaries + kernels). A FastViT student can carry the same cheap CRF head; the head's cost is independent of the backbone.
error_correlation_with_ours: Moderate: same backbone and inputs, so errors stay correlated on truly ambiguous wells, but the decisions on blend / jump columns change systematically; a CRF-head model is a reasonable blend member with the plain ConvNeXt, and more diverse than a second seed.
risk: (1) The ConvNeXt's receptive field may already capture most continuity, so the learned transitions add little (the model can learn a flat kernel). (2) A first-order chain cannot fix band confusion where both bands are smoothly reachable; the metric-optimal answer there is a hedge, which we already output. (3) CRF NLL on the true path is mode-seeking-ish in training and can sharpen marginals; prefer marginal/expectation losses. (4) Training-time sequential loop and numerical stability in log space. (5) The AnchorCNN precedent: a trained path model at 5.94 ft is worse than the per-column U-Net, though for backbone and normalisation reasons, not proof against structure. (6) Our ablations at 60 epochs (axial attention, RAFT, AcfNet) were all null; a 150-epoch comparison with two seeds is needed to resolve effects near 0.39 ft.
notes: Why the post-hoc decode failed and the trained one might not: the forward-backward product assumes emissions are conditionally independent given the state, but U-Net column posteriors share almost all of their evidence with their neighbours; multiplying 345 of them with a smoothness prior raises the effective confidence enormously. Training end-to-end removes this by letting the unaries carry only the evidence not explained by the chain. Closest analogues in stereo: SGM-Nets (learned DP penalties) and hybrid CNN-CRF (end-to-end structured SVM). The soft-DTW divergence fixes soft-DTW's self-similarity bias if a DTW-type loss is ever used for typewell-to-lateral GR alignment. Related items: A03 (DTW), A04 (DP patents), A15 (explicit dip state), B06 (differentiable particle filters), B08 (retinal layer graph-search CNNs).
